behaviour: The clock is a TextClock in the location's time zone; it is right every minute between updates.
Night track: from Isya until Subuh the bar runs Isya to Subuh (two stops).
Header keeps today's date after Isya though the next prayer is tomorrow.
Clock, times, names, countdown, Hijri date and footer never ellipsize; dates and place may (WidgetFitTest).
Countdown minutes round up ('1 menit' until the prayer).
Short cards keep the scale's names first: one-line countdown ('Jumat' if needed), clock down to 85%, then names drop.

glass.sheen: linear, top left to 0.6w,h: 6% -> 2% at 0.4 -> 3% white
glass.edge: 1dp, 40% white at the top -> 12% at 0.35 -> 8% at the bottom
glass.contrast: muted text >= 4.5:1 over a white wallpaper (GlassContrastTest)

celestial.sun: NASA/SDO HMI continuum photo, limb darkening restored (I = 1 - 0.32(1 - mu)), warmer centre, redder limb, orange glow
celestial.moon: NASA CGI Moon Kit LROC colour map on a sphere, gamma 1.8, Lommel-Seeliger lighting for the phase, 3% earthshine
celestial.phase: mean synodic month from the 2000-01-06 18:14 UTC new moon (Moon.phase)
celestial.shown: sun from sunrise to Maghrib, moon otherwise; Card layouts only

narrative.overview:
The widget is a pane of translucent black glass over the wallpaper. The largest thing on it is the time now, a live clock in bold. Under it one line says how long until the next prayer and names that prayer and its time in yellow. On the right, the sun by day or the moon at its real phase by night. A bar under them shows how far the day (or the night) has gone, with the prayers' names and times as its scale.

The large figure used to be the next prayer's time, which people read as the current time. Now the clock is the clock, and a prayer time only ever appears with its name beside it.
keyCharacteristics: Translucent black glass (74%) with a faint sheen and a lit top edge; the wallpaper shows through.
One accent (`accent-signal`), used only for what is next: the prayer and its time, its scale stop, the bar's fill, tomorrow's fast.
The current time is a TextClock the launcher keeps.
The sun and the moon are drawn from NASA imagery, the moon lit for tonight's phase.
Text never ellipsizes where it carries the answer; it shrinks first.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The accent marks what is next and nothing else. A new element gets the accent only if it points forward in time.

rules.name: The Glass Not Paint Rule
rules.body: The glass is translucent and never opaque; the wallpaper must show through it. Contrast is held by its darkness, measured over a white wallpaper.

rules.name: The Clock Is the Clock Rule
rules.body: The large figure is always the current time. A prayer time is never shown large or alone: it always sits beside its prayer's name.

rules.name: The No Ellipsis on the Answer Rule
rules.body: The clock, times, prayer names, the countdown line, the Hijri date and footer lines shrink to fit and never end in '…'. WidgetFitTest enforces it.

rules.name: The Figures Take the Room Rule
rules.body: Spare space goes to the clock and the countdown, never to wider padding or bigger gaps.

rules.name: The Glass Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from the glass's tint, sheen and edge. No drop shadows and no lifted layers.

dos: Make the large figure the current time, and put every prayer time beside its name.
Give the accent only to what is next.
Shrink type through the fit factors before anything that carries the answer ellipsizes; keep WidgetFitTest green.
Keep the glass dark enough for muted text at 4.5:1 over a white wallpaper (GlassContrastTest).
Take every gap and padding from the shared spacing steps.
donts: List the five times as a table or list.
Let the countdown reach the size of the clock.
Make the glass opaque or add drop shadows.
Let text run under the sun or the moon.
Apply the app's Material 3 palettes to the widget, or the widget's tokens to app screens.
